jcr:content.jcr:description: A fictional ten-club league used to demonstrate the Kestros sport-league sample site.

subtitle.text: A fictional ten-club league used as a Kestros demo site. Every number, name, and fixture on this site is made up - the structure is what matters.

body.text:
What this site is.

This is a demonstration of a sport-league website built on Kestros. The templates are deliberately generic - the same HTL and CSS render basketball, hockey, cricket, or any other league-based sport. Only the datasources differ.

What is hand-authored.

On the current site, every team, match, and player is a literal JCR content node. You can see them in the JCR resolver at /content/sites/league-demo.

What datasources would feed.

In a real deployment, every list on this site would be replaced with a single content-area datasource:

  • Standings table - standings-for-season datasource. Rows and column labels come from the sport rule set.
  • Schedule - fixtures-for-season grouped by matchweek.
  • Teams index + team detail - a single kes:dynamic-page template with a team-by-slug lookup, so every club renders from one template.
  • Player detail + match detail - same dynamic-page pattern, with player-by-slug and match-by-id datasources.
  • Column labels - "Goals", "Assists", "Clean sheets" - come from a stat-schema the datasource exposes alongside the rows. Swap the schema, swap the sport.

What is next.

Once the datasources are in place, this page will stay identical. The content nodes will just be replaced by a datasource reference and the dynamic page template will take over.
